full_judgment:
34. In the case of Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain vs State reported in 65 DLR 1, the High Court Division held as under—"Since there are prima-facie allegations against the accused-petitioner attracting ingredients of both the offences and he is under legal obligation to clear his position and account for in respect of possession of properties allegedly disproportionate to his known source of income to the satisfaction of the Court at the time of trial having onus to rebut presumption of guilt under section 27(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, there is nothing to be prejudiced if the trial of the case is allowed to continue." 

 40. The similar :view has been taken in the case of HM Ershad vs State reported in 45 DLR 533 wherein the High Court Division held—"14.—On interpretation of sections 241A and 242 of CrPC we find that the court has jurisdiction to pass an order of discharge if he is satisfied that the charge is groundless and if he finds so, he has to give reason but in framing charge it is not required for him to record reasons showing that there are grounds for framing charge, it is enough if the court is of opinion that there is ground for presumption that the accused has committed the offence. The formation of such opinion is dependent only on the application of judicial mind based on materials collected from the record of the case."
